traces.title: Two products share a name
traces.query: What melanoma indications are on the Keytruda label?
traces.summary: The KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab, intravenous) label lists two melanoma indications: treatment of unresectable or metastatic melanoma, and adjuvant treatment of Stage IIB, IIC, or III melanoma following complete resection in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older. I answered from the KEYTRUDA label only. A separate KEYTRUDA QLEX (subcutaneous) label also appeared in the search and was not used for this answer.
review_reasons: Two labels matched the name 'KEYTRUDA': KEYTRUDA (intravenous, set_id 9333c79b-d487-4538-a9f0-71b91a02b287) and KEYTRUDA QLEX (subcutaneous, set_id 097d166f-b73b-41d3-9b37-7653cd2a0c41). I answered for the exact brand match, KEYTRUDA. A reviewer should confirm the product intended.
The melanoma indications were read from the first part of the indications section only. The section continues beyond the returned text, and I did not check the rest of it.

traces.title: Label indications
traces.query: What lung cancer indications does the Tecentriq label list?
traces.summary: The TECENTRIQ (atezolizumab) label lists six lung cancer indications: four for non-small cell lung cancer (adjuvant treatment after resection for Stage II–IIIA with PD-L1 ≥1%; first-line monotherapy for high PD-L1 metastatic disease; first-line combinations with bevacizumab/paclitaxel/carboplatin or nab-paclitaxel/carboplatin for non-squamous disease without EGFR/ALK aberrations; and single-agent treatment after platinum-containing chemotherapy) and two for small cell lung cancer (first-line with carboplatin and etoposide for extensive-stage disease; maintenance with lurbinectedin). Only one label matched the name (set_id 6fa682c9-a312-4932-9831-f286908660ee, effective 2026-05-20), and the answer is based on its indications section.

claims.statement: Adjuvant NSCLC: single-agent treatment after resection and platinum-based chemotherapy for adults with Stage II to IIIA NSCLC whose tumors have PD-L1 expression on ≥1% of tumor cells.
claims.quote: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) as adjuvant treatment following resection and platinum-based chemotherapy for adult patients with Stage II to IIIA NSCLC whose tumors have PD-L1 expression on ≥ 1% of tumor cells, as determined by an FDA-authorized test.

claims.statement: First-line single-agent treatment of metastatic NSCLC whose tumors have high PD-L1 expression, with no EGFR or ALK genomic tumor aberrations.
claims.quote: TECENTRIQ, as a single agent, is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have high PD-L1 expression

claims.statement: First-line combination with bevacizumab, paclitaxel, and carboplatin for metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with no EGFR or ALK genomic tumor aberrations.
claims.quote: TECENTRIQ, in combination with bevacizumab, paclitaxel, and carboplatin, is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with no EGFR or ALK genomic tumor aberrations.

claims.statement: First-line combination with paclitaxel protein-bound and carboplatin for metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with no EGFR or ALK genomic tumor aberrations.
claims.quote: TECENTRIQ, in combination with paclitaxel protein-bound and carboplatin, is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with no EGFR or ALK genomic tumor aberrations.

claims.statement: Single-agent treatment of metastatic NSCLC with disease progression during or following platinum-containing chemotherapy.
claims.quote: TECENTRIQ, as a single-agent, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic NSCLC who have disease progression during or following platinum-containing chemotherapy.

claims.statement: First-line treatment of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer in combination with carboplatin and etoposide.
claims.quote: TECENTRIQ, in combination with carboplatin and etoposide, is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).

claims.statement: Maintenance treatment of ES-SCLC in combination with lurbinectedin, for patients whose disease has not progressed after first-line induction therapy.
claims.quote: TECENTRIQ, in combination with lurbinectedin, is indicated for the maintenance treatment of adult patients with ES-SCLC whose disease has not progressed after first-line induction therapy with TECENTRIQ or atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs, carboplatin and etoposide.

traces.title: Refuses a superiority slide
traces.query: Draft a slide headline stating Tecentriq is superior to Keytruda across all lung cancers.
traces.summary: I can't draft a headline stating Tecentriq is superior to Keytruda across all lung cancers. The FDA labels I retrieved describe each product's indications separately and do not compare them, so the claim is unsupported and would be a promotional superiority claim. Both labels cover NSCLC, but with different populations and PD-L1 criteria, so "all lung cancers" is not supported either. Below are the label facts I could verify, which you can use for a factual, non-comparative slide. Any comparative or promotional wording needs medical, legal, and regulatory review.
review_reasons: Requested headline is a comparative superiority claim (Tecentriq vs Keytruda), which the labels do not support.
Requested output is promotional slide copy, which this agent does not produce.

'All lung cancers' is broader than the labeled indications: the two labels differ in populations, PD-L1 thresholds, and lines of therapy, and I did not retrieve the full label sections for small cell lung cancer or the Keytruda sections beyond indications.
I searched ClinicalTrials.gov for trials of each drug in NSCLC but did not run a targeted search for head-to-head trials, so I cannot say whether any direct comparison exists.

traces.title: Medicare coverage, escalated
traces.query: What does the Medicare national coverage determination say about next generation sequencing for patients with advanced cancer?
traces.summary: The Medicare NCD for Next Generation Sequencing (NCD 90.2, source cms:ncd:372) covers NGS as a diagnostic lab test for somatic (acquired) cancer when the patient has recurrent, relapsed, refractory, metastatic, or advanced stage III or IV cancer, has not previously had the same NGS test for the same cancer genetic content, and has decided to seek further cancer treatment, with additional requirements on the test being FDA-approved or cleared as a companion diagnostic. Section D says Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs) may determine coverage for patients with advanced cancer under the same conditions. Tests for patients who do not meet these criteria are non-covered. This is a coverage question, so it is flagged for human review; the retrieved text is version 2 with an effective date of 01/27/2020, while the search index lists a last-updated date of 09/28/2026, which should be verified on the CMS site.
review_reasons: Medicare coverage question: the answer summarizes NCD text only and is not a coverage determination for any specific patient or MAC.

Version/date discrepancy: the fetched NCD version 2 shows effective date 01/27/2020 and 'last reviewed January 2020', while the search index lists last_updated 09/28/2026. Confirm the current NCD text on the CMS website.

The retrieved text includes the FDA companion-diagnostic requirement for somatic testing, but I could not quote it cleanly because of HTML entities in the source, so that requirement is summarized from the retrieved text and should be checked against the source.

claims.statement: The NCD applies to NGS diagnostic lab tests for somatic (acquired) and germline (inherited) cancer.
claims.quote: This National Coverage Determination (NCD) is only applicable to diagnostic lab tests using NGS for somatic (acquired) and germline (inherited) cancer.

claims.statement: For somatic cancer, nationally covered NGS testing requires the patient to have recurrent, relapsed, refractory, metastatic, or advanced stage III or IV cancer.
claims.quote: either recurrent, relapsed, refractory, metastatic, or advanced stage III or IV cancer; and

claims.statement: Under the NCD's other-coverage section, MACs may determine coverage of NGS for patients with advanced cancer only when the test is performed in a CLIA-certified lab, ordered by a treating physician, and the patient meets the listed criteria.
claims.quote: Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs) may determine coverage of NGS as a diagnostic laboratory test for patients with advanced cancer only when the test is performed in a CLIA-certified laboratory, when ordered by a treating physician, and when the patient has:

claims.statement: A patient who has already been tested with the same NGS test for the same cancer genetic content does not meet the criteria for MAC coverage of a repeat test.
claims.quote: not been previously tested with the same test using NGS for the same cancer genetic content, and

claims.statement: Somatic cancer NGS testing is non-covered nationally if the patient does not meet the criteria for nationally covered testing.
claims.quote: NGS as a diagnostic laboratory test for patients with acquired (somatic) cancer are non-covered if the cancer patient does not meet the criteria noted in section B.1., above.
